- **Fields without a term** comes from the failing rules of the latest run, so it changes as rules start or stop failing.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text:
- **Data owner** (approve): edit, approve and mark terms as reviewed.
- **Data steward**: draft terms with Add terms from the rule library, comment on terms.
- **Everyone**: read, search, comment, export.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.text:
- `j` and `k` move, `Enter` opens a term.
- `Esc` closes the inspector.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **A term stays Under review**: it waits for the object's owner. People shows who owns the object.
- **No owner shown**: the object has no owner yet. Administration, Stewardship lists the gaps.
- **A field is missing from Fields without a term**: only fields read by failing rules are listed.

chapters.title: Lineage
chapters.summary: From source table to field to rule to the S/4 feature it blocks, and the related objects to fix first.
captions: Lineage draws why a failing value matters.
From the source table, to the field, to the rule, to the S/4 feature it blocks.
Hover or focus a node to read its facts.
Features come from the impact model of the current run.
Export as SVG for a slide or a document.
Related objects in the header: fix the upstream one first.
The lineage draws the failing rules with the highest value at risk, so the drawing stays readable.
The same features appear on the Readiness tab: blocked and degraded in S/4HANA.
Each feature names the rules behind it, so you know which fix releases it.
Open a feature to read what it does and which records hold it back.

sections.text: Lineage draws why a failing value matters: from the source table, to the field, to the rule that fails on it, to the S/4 feature it blocks or degrades. The **Lineage** tab of an object draws it for the failing rules with the highest value at risk. Open it from the object's tabs, for example `/o/ecc-production/material-master/lineage`.

sections.heading: What is on it
sections.text:
- **Four columns**: **Source tables** (`MARA`, `MARC`, `MBEW`), **Fields** (`MARA-MEINS`), **Rules** (`MM142`) and **S/4 features** (Migration cockpit: material load, Material ledger actual costing, Embedded EWM product master and so on).
- **Node facts**: "Hover or focus a node to see its facts here. Click a rule or a feature to open it."
- **Export as SVG**: the drawing as a file for a slide or a document.
- The line under it: "Drawn from the 8 failing rules of Material master with the highest value at risk. Features come from the impact model of the current run."

sections.heading: Related objects
sections.text: The object header lists the related objects with their relation, **upstream** or **downstream**. An upstream object's failures pass into this one, so the Work ledger and the record inspector say which to fix first, for example "Fix Material master first: 3,640 upstream failures. Records there fail before this object can pass."

sections.heading: The numbers and where they come from
sections.text:
- The rules drawn are the failing rules of this object in the current run, highest value at risk first.
- The features and whether each is blocked or degraded come from the feature impact rules of the run: the same mapping the Readiness tab shows.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text: - **Everyone**: read, open a rule or a feature, export as SVG.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.text: - `Tab` moves through the nodes; the node facts follow the focus. `Enter` opens a rule or a feature.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **The drawing is empty**: no rule of this object fails in the current run, or the object has no run.
- **A feature you expect is missing**: no impact rule maps the failing rules to it. Impact rules are shipped with Meridian; ask your administrator.

chapters.title: Processes and the designer
chapters.summary: Which process steps the data blocks, what fixing a rule would release, handing a rule off, and editing the process model.
captions: Processes shows which business process steps this object's data blocks.
2 of 4 process steps are blocked by Material master: PTP step 3, PP step 1.
A blocked step names the activity, the field, its pass rate and failing records.
What if these rules were fixed: tick rules and see which steps would be ready.
Nothing is changed and no data is read.
Open a step to hand its blocking rule to a steward.
The process designer: the model, its levels, and the fields each activity reads.
Save as a new version, then publish. The Processes tab shows it on the next run.
Versions keep every saved model with what changed.

sections.text: The **Processes** tab of an object shows which business process steps its data blocks: Procure to Pay, Plan to Produce, Order to Cash and the others, down to the step, the transaction and the field. The **process designer** is where the process model is edited. Open the tab from the object's tabs (`/o/{system}/{object}/processes`) and the designer with **Open the designer** (`.../processes/design`).

sections.heading: What is on the Processes tab
sections.text:
- **The sentence**: "2 of 4 process steps are blocked by Material master: PTP step 3, PP step 1."
- **Each process**: its name and code ("Procure to Pay PTP"), its state ("Blocked, 1 of 3 steps blocked"), its description and its steps. Each step names the transaction (`ME51N`, `ME21N`, `MIGO`), its state (**Ready** or **Blocked**) and, when blocked, the activities and fields behind it with status, pass rate and failing records, for example "Enter Quantity and Unit: `MARA-MEINS` Base unit of measure, Blocked, 94.1%, 3,640".
- The rule under it, as the product states it: "A step is blocked when a field it writes fails a critical or high rule, or passes under 70%. Failing counts are records, and a record can fail several rules."
- **What if these rules were fixed** (simulation): "Tick the rules to fix. The steps of Material master are read again without their failures; nothing is changed and no data is read." Each rule shows "3,640 records at least, in 1 step". The result shows which steps would be ready.
- **Process designer** with **Open the designer**.

sections.heading: The step inspector
sections.text: Open a step for its transaction, its activities and fields, the rules failing on them and **Hand off**, which hands a blocking rule to a steward with a note.

sections.heading: The process designer
sections.text:
"Process designer, Material master", with the model's state, for example "Draft, version 1, updated 12 Oct 2026".

- **Model**: choose a model, **Create a model** (start from the reference model or the group model), **Publish model**, **Rename model**, **Delete model**.
- **The tree**: levels L1 to L4 (for example Procure to pay, Sourcing, Purchase order, Create purchase order with its activities), each with **Up**, **Down** and **Delete**, and **Add a process at the top level**.
- **The model panel**: "Choose an item in the tree to rename it, reorder it, add what sits under it, or map fields to its activities."
- **What changed**, **Save as a new version**, **Discard changes**, and **Versions**.
- The rule at the foot: "A step is blocked in process readiness when a field it reads fails a critical or high rule. Map the fields each activity reads here, and the Processes tab shows them on the next run."

sections.heading: The numbers and where they come from
sections.text:
- Step states come from the fields mapped to each activity and the rules that failed on those fields in the run.
- The what-if simulation is computed in the browser over the process document and the receipt; it reads no data and changes nothing.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text:
- **Process analyst**: read readiness, run what-if, hand off a blocking rule (handoff rule), export the as-is process (export process), edit and publish the model.
- **Data steward**: receive handed-off rules in Work.
- **Everyone**: read.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.text:
- `j` and `k` move through steps, `Enter` opens a step.
- In the designer tree, `Tab` moves between items.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **"Choose at least one rule."** The simulation needs a ticked rule.
- **Every step is Ready but the object is No-go**: the failing rules are on fields no activity reads. Map them in the designer.
- **Your edits do not show on the Processes tab**: they show on the next run, and only once the model is published.

chapters.title: Reports and schedules
chapters.summary: Reports built from a stored run, and schedules that build and send them on a rhythm.
captions: Reports are built from stored runs, so a number in a report matches the run it names.
Every report: its run, format, who made it and the download.
Schedules build a report from the latest run and send it.
Open a schedule: report, which run, cadence, recipients.
Run it now, pause, or delete. Files already made stay in the list.
Create a report from any run.
Choose the report and the run it is built from.
Reports come from a run: the board pack, the analyst workbook, the analysis and trend reports, the rule catalogue.
A schedule that partly delivered or failed says so in Last result.
Channels that can take reports are set under Administration, Alerts.

sections.text: Reports are files built from a stored run: the board pack, the analyst workbook, the analysis report, the trend report and the rule catalogue. Schedules build a report from the latest run and send it on a rhythm. Open Reports from the command line (type "reports") or at `/reports`.

sections.heading: What is on it
sections.text:
- **The sentence**: "6 reports made, 2 of 3 schedules are on. Reports are built from stored runs, so a number in a report matches the run it names."
- **Create a report** and **Schedule a report**.
- **Reports**: report, run ("Run of 16 Oct 2026"), format (PDF or XLSX), created, by, size and **Download**. The rule catalogue is "Not tied to a run".
- **Schedules**: "Each builds a report from the latest run and sends it." Report and format, cadence ("Every Monday at 07:00 (Africa/Johannesburg)"), recipients, next run and last result (**Delivered**, **Partly delivered**, **Failed** or "Not run yet"), and **Paused** for a paused schedule.

sections.heading: Create a report
sections.text: Choose the report, the run it is built from ("Built from the run you choose") and, optionally, one object. The report is built by a worker and appears in the list when it is ready.

sections.heading: The schedule inspector
sections.text: Open a schedule for its facts (next run, last run and its result), then: name, report (Board pack (PDF), Analyst workbook (XLSX), Analysis report (PDF), Trend report (PDF), Rule catalogue (PDF)), **Which run** ("The latest finished run", "The latest file upload" or the latest run of one system), an optional object, the cadence (every day, week or month, the day and the time in the tenant's time zone), the recipients (people of the tenant and the alert channels that take reports) and **Schedule is on**. Actions: **Save the schedule**, **Pause**, **Run it now** ("It is built on the worker and delivered to the recipients; the next scheduled run is unchanged.") and **Delete** ("No more reports are built or sent from this schedule. Files it already made stay in the list.").

sections.heading: The numbers and where they come from
sections.text: Every figure in a report is read from the run it names, so the board pack of 16 Oct says what the landscape said for that run. Money is in the tenant currency from the run's cost model. Alerts and channel messages carry counts, rule ids and links, never record values.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text:
- **Programme lead, analyst, admin** (export): create, schedule, run now, pause, delete.
- **Everyone with view**: download reports. "Creating and scheduling reports needs the export permission."
- **Administrator**: add the channels that can receive reports under Administration, Alerts.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.text:
- `j` and `k` move through reports and schedules, `Enter` opens a schedule.
- `Esc` closes the inspector.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **"No report has been made yet. Create one from a run, or schedule one to arrive on its own."**
- **"No one can receive reports yet."** Invite people, or add an email or Teams channel under Administration, Alerts.
- **Partly delivered**: one recipient or channel refused it. Check the channel under Administration, Alerts; email needs an email backend, which Administration, Platform and updates reports under Health checks.
- **Failed**: open the schedule and choose **Run it now** after fixing the channel; the job appears under Runs, Jobs.

chapters.title: Waves and gates
chapters.summary: Migration waves with their verdict counts, gate criteria and readiness certificate, and assigning objects to waves.
captions: A wave is a set of objects moved together in one cutover.
Each wave: due date, go, at risk and no-go counts, and the gate state.
The next step follows the nearest wave.
Edit opens the migration waves panel.
Name, target date and stage: plan, mock loads, dress rehearsal, cutover.
The gate: min score, zero criticals, contracts met, each with what fails it now.
The readiness certificate is not signed in this version; its link shows the checks.
Assign each object to a wave, then save the changes.

sections.text: A migration wave is a set of objects moved together in one cutover, with a target date, a stage and a gate: the conditions every object must meet before the wave may go. The landscape's **Waves** view shows each wave with its verdict counts and gate state; the **Migration waves** panel is where the programme lead plans waves and sets gates. Open the view with **Waves** on the landscape (`/?view=waves`) and the panel with **Edit** on a wave (`?open=waves:{id}`), which opens that wave first with its gate on top and the other waves collapsed.

sections.heading: The Waves view
sections.text:
Each wave heading reads, for example, "Wave 1: finance foundations, due 16 Nov 2026, 1 go, 0 at risk, 3 no-go, Gate not passed, 2 of 3 not met", with **Edit** and **Certificate**. At phone width the heading stays above each wave's objects, with the same gate state and both links. Under it, the wave's objects with their ruler, score, verdict, records and rules. The programme lead's next-step button follows the nearest wave: "Clear the 3 no-go objects in Wave 1: finance foundations" with "Wave 1: finance foundations: due 16 Nov 2026, in 17 days. 1 go, 0 at risk, 3 no-go."

An object's own **Readiness** tab lists its waves with the verdict, blocking gaps, score, readiness and records blocked, and the gate's threshold in the same words as the gate ("Gate: min score 85.0"). An object no run has scored yet for its wave shows no readiness or records blocked; the tab says so instead of showing zeros.

sections.heading: The Migration waves panel
sections.text:
For each wave: **Name**, **Target date**, **Stage** (Plan, Mock load 1, Mock load 2, Dress rehearsal, Cutover) and its sign-off state ("Not signed off.").

**Gate**: up to three conditions, each with what fails it now:

- **Min score**: "Gate: min score 85.0", with the objects below it. The same words appear on the Readiness tab and the Waves view.
- **Zero criticals**: "No critical rule over tolerance", with the objects capped by a critical rule.
- **Contracts met**: "Data contracts met", or "No active contract names these objects."

**Save the gate** stores it. "No gate yet: a wave without one moves on its verdict alone."

**Readiness certificate**: the latest issued version and its state, for example "Version 2, waiting for signatures" or "Version 2, signed", or "Not issued". **Open the certificate** opens it: issue a new version, sign it, or download the PDF. When the gate refuses an issue, the certificate lists each object in the way, linked to its page, with the rules that stop it.

**Add a wave** creates one; **Objects** assigns each object to a wave or to none; **Save changes** or **Discard**. **Delete** removes a wave.

sections.heading: The numbers and where they come from
sections.text:
- **Go, at risk, no-go** counts are the verdicts of the wave's objects in the run in the top bar, from the score bands.
- **Gate state** checks each condition against the same run: the shown scores, the critical rules over tolerance, and the active contracts that name the objects.
- **Due in N days** counts from today to the target date.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text:
- **Programme lead** (analyse): plan waves, set gates, assign objects.
- **Data owner**: read the gate state of their objects' waves.
- **Everyone**: read the Waves view.
- **Sign off** (approve): on each wave in the Migration waves panel, once its verdict is go. The panel shows who signed it off and when; any later change to the wave clears the sign-off.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.text:
- `g` then `l`, then the **Waves** view switch.
- `Esc` closes the panel.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **A wave shows every object no-go but scores look close to target**: the cap holds them. The gate's **Zero criticals** line names the objects; clear their critical rules first.
- **Contracts met says no contract names the objects**: create one in People, Data contracts, or remove the condition.
- **The certificate says "Not issued"**: no version is issued yet. Open the certificate and issue one once the gate passes; if it refuses, the list under the button names the objects and rules to clear.

chapters.title: Administration
chapters.summary: Users, roles, sign-in, view as, share links, licence, settings, stewardship, configuration bundle, data, notifications, start and schedule, and the platform.
captions: Administration: everything that sets up this tenant.
Users: seats, roles as grants, invitations.
Roles and permissions: built-in roles are fixed; copy one to change it.
Single sign-on with OpenID Connect, and the sign-in page rules.
View as a role: read-only, for support, and in the audit log.
Licence: status, seats, validity and the modules this deployment may use.
Settings: weights, score bands, the cap rule and tolerance, cost model and retention.
One critical rule beyond its tolerance holds an object at 85; two or more at 70. The caps are fixed.
Stewardship: one owner per object, stewards per slice, and the gaps.
Configuration bundle: export the configuration as one file; import with a diff first.
Rules import and export: imported rules land as drafts, never live.
Audit log: every change, by whom and when, and every call to the language model.
Alerts: channels and thresholds. Alerts never carry record values.
Default digest: the summary the tenant gets by default. Each person sets their own in Preferences.
Start and schedule: start an extraction, an analysis, a configuration load or an upload, and schedule them.
Platform and updates: jobs, the platform version, health checks and the diagnostics bundle.

sections.text: Administration is everything that sets up the tenant: who can sign in, what the licence covers, how scoring and alerts behave, and the state of the platform. It opens from your account menu, **Administration**, for anyone who holds an administrative permission, at `/admin`. "Everything that sets up this tenant: who can sign in, what the licence covers, how scoring and alerts behave, and the state of the platform. Each section opens in this column." You see only the sections your role opens; the rest say which permission they need.

sections.heading: People and access
sections.text:
- **Users**: "7 of 25 seats. A person's roles are grants: open a row to add or remove them." **Invite a user**, **Import users**, filters by role and status (Invited, Invite expired, Active, Locked, Suspended). A banner warns about invitations older than 7 days. Opening a person shows their grants, what they can do now and every action on the account. Needs manage users.
- **Roles and permissions**: "Built-in roles cannot be changed. Copy one to start a custom role, then set exactly what it may do. Give a role for one system or object only, from a person's grants." The matrix "What each role may do", **Access requests** (grant, or decline with a reason the person reads) and recent changes.
- **Single sign-on**: OpenID Connect with your identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, Okta). Issuer address, client ID, client secret ("Stored encrypted and never shown again."), button name, the redirect address to register, **Test sign-in** and **Turn off single sign-on**. "People who sign in for the first time get the Viewer role and no access grants; give them access under Users."
- **Sign-in page**: the button name, allowed email domains, **Require single sign-on** ("Password sign-in stops for everyone except administrators, who keep it as a way in if the provider is down."), and the fixed password rules: "At least 12 characters, not the email name, and not a common password"; "10 failed sign-ins lock the account for 15 minutes".
- **View as a role**: "See the product as one role sees it, to answer a support question or check a role before you grant it. Everything is read-only while you view as a role, and starting and stopping are in the audit log." The top bar shows "Viewing as" until you stop.
- **Share links**: "Read-only links to one page, opened as a viewer by people of this tenant until they expire. Revoke one and it stops working at once."
- **Out of office**: "Who is away and who covers their approvals and assigned work. Each person sets their own from Preferences; an administrator can end one."
- **Approval workflows**: who approves fix batches and change requests, in which order, and when a step applies. Each workflow lists its versions with the active one marked. Edit the definition of the next version as JSON, try it with **Dry run** on sample facts (which steps apply, the approvers and how long each has), then **Save as a new version**, active at once or not. **Activate** an older version to go back to it; approvals already under way keep the version they started with. Needs manage workflows.
- **API keys**: "A key acts as its own service account with only the roles you give it, and shows in the audit log under its name. The key itself is shown once, when you create it."

sections.heading: Tenant
sections.text:
- **Licence**: company, status, tier, seats, validity, last checked, platform version and the licensed modules and features. **Check with Meridian HQ now**. "Plan changes and invoices are handled in Meridian HQ; this deployment keeps its data either way." Every licence is verified against the vendor's Ed25519 key built into the image. When Meridian HQ cannot be reached, the last valid signed answer is honoured for 14 days after it was signed: the page still reads Valid while the API reports the status `offline_grace` with the days left; after that, gated pages lock until Meridian HQ answers again.
- **Billing**: resolved exceptions by billing tier on top of the base fee; read only.
- **Settings**: the tenant; **Dimension weights** ("The score is each measured dimension times its weight. The weights must add up to 100." **Use the DAMA defaults**); **Score bands** ("At or above target is on target (go), at or above warning is at risk, below that is failing."); **Cap rule and tolerance**: "One critical rule failing beyond its tolerance holds that object at 85; two or more hold it at 70. The caps are fixed. The tolerance says how many failing records count as beyond.", with **Failing share, percent** and **Failing records** and the severity weights and multipliers; **Cost model and currency**; **Planner assumptions**; **Retention** (keep runs, reports and audit rows for so many days, keep the baseline; purges rehearse first and the purge log records each one); **Delete all data**, which issues a token that works after 24 hours. **Sandbox mode**: **Enter sandbox mode** copies the latest finished run into a sandbox run; until **Exit sandbox mode**, decisions land on the copy only, decisions on the real run are refused with the reason ("Sandbox mode is on: decisions apply to the sandbox run only."), and notifications, webhooks, digests, report mailouts and write-backs are held back and counted. A band across every page says "Sandbox: nothing leaves this deployment." with since when and by whom. Entering and exiting need manage system; exiting discards the sandbox runs.
- **Stewardship**: "One accountable owner per object and one steward per company code, plant or organisation." The template per object (owner role, owner, stewards by slice, steward, teams), **Save the template**, **Check what applying does** (a dry-run diff), **Apply**, and **Gaps**: "Every object needs one owner and at least one steward per active slice", for example "Vendor master (AP): No steward for purchasing organisation 1000".
- **Configuration bundle**: "Rules switched on or off, field mappings, waves and their gates, settings, SLA policies and the escalation chain as one JSON file." **Download the bundle**; import with a diff first: "Import adds and changes; it never deletes what the file leaves out. Check the diff first."

sections.heading: Data
sections.text:
- **Field mappings**: "Name the column in your files that holds each standard SAP field, then save the row." **Reset all to defaults**.
- **Reference data**: postal code and bank code (SWIFT BIC) lists per system. "Until a list is loaded those rules check the format only." An upload replaces the system's current list.
- **Rules import and export**: "Every rule of the tenant as YAML or Excel, and many rules at once back in. Imported rules are validated against the data dictionary and land as drafts for review, never live." **Check the file**, then **Create drafts**.
- **Policy packs**: GxP, SOX and GDPR. Each pack names field classes, the authority each answers to (an article or section, such as "SOX Section 404(a) (controls over changes to vendor payment data)") and the catalogue rules that evidence it. A card per pack shows fields classified, rules evidencing, rules measured, failing records and classes breached, and whether it is applied. **Apply the pack** and **Remove the pack** need manage rules. Open a pack for its classes, their fields and the evidence of each rule, for the current state or one run. An applied class with a failing critical rule is a policy breach: a filled shield beside the score on the landscape cell, the ruler and the object's receipt, which names the class, its authority and the rules.
- **Audit log**: every change, who made it, the object and the result, filters by person, action, object kind and dates, **Export CSV** and **Export Excel**, and **AI calls**: "Every call to the language model: which service, how long, and whether a deterministic rule answered first. Prompts and records are never stored here."

sections.heading: Notifications
sections.text:
- **Alerts**: channels (email, Microsoft Teams, signed webhook) with their digest, board pack and critical alerts; **When to alert** (critical and high failing rules, score drop in points) and **Score floors per object**. "Alerts carry counts, rule ids and links, never record values."
- **Default digest**: the tenant's default digest. Each person sets their own under Preferences.
- **Digests**: scheduled summaries for a role (the programme lead every Monday at 07:00) or a migration wave: the landscape sentence, score moves, the waves and their gates, approvals waiting, SLA breaches and the top value at risk. The form takes the cadence (a preset or a cron line, checked as you type), the time zone, the channel (email with addresses and people, an alert channel, or the `digest.sent` webhook event), **Attach the digest as a PDF** and **Send on its schedule**. In the digest's inspector: **Send now**, **Preview** (the email in a sealed frame, or the numbers it is built from), **Pause**, **Edit**, **Delete** and the delivery log. Needs manage settings.

sections.heading: Operations
sections.text:
- **Start and schedule** (the runs themselves are on Runs): start an extraction (objects, company codes, plants, document dates, analyse straight after), start an analysis of a stored extraction, load the configuration, scheduled runs, **Upload a file** (a CSV, TSV, Excel, JSON or Parquet file of one object becomes a run and is analysed at once; its columns are matched by the field mappings; needs upload) and recent jobs with **Retry**.
- **Platform and updates**: jobs by state and kind, the platform version and **Update to** the latest when Meridian HQ knows one, **Health checks** (database, cache and queue, background workers, licence, email delivery, file storage): "Each check says what it found and what needs fixing. They refresh every 30 seconds.", and **Support** with **Download diagnostics bundle**: versions, health checks, recent errors and configuration with every secret removed, and no SAP record values.

sections.heading: Provisioning, theming and compliance
sections.text:
- **Provisioning (SCIM)**, under Users: "Microsoft Entra ID, Okta and other identity providers create, update and suspend people here through SCIM 2.0. Give them the base URL and a token." **Create a token**, **Rotate the token** (the old one stops at once), **Revoke**, and **Group to role**: "A person in one of these identity provider groups gets its role. Saving re-syncs everyone in a SCIM group at once." Only grants SCIM made are removed, and the last active administrator is never left without admin.
- **Appearance**, under Settings: the tenant's accent, logo and name, with the contrast of the accent checked before it is saved.
- **Compliance**, under Settings: data residency, retention days per table family, encryption flags and the last backup.

sections.heading: Sign-in, audit and tenancy
sections.text:
- The first sign-in of an account that must change its password (the seeded administrator, or an account an administrator reset) goes to the password change before anything else.
- The audit log records sign-in, failed sign-in, lockout, sign-out and password change (`auth.login`, `auth.login_failed`, `auth.lockout`, `auth.logout`, `auth.password_change`), and single sign-on (`auth.sso_login`, `auth.sso_refused`, `auth.sso_user_created`). A failed sign-in keeps the email as typed and the reason, never the password.
- A signed-in request runs in the tenant its verified token names; the deployment's own tenant is set by `MERIDIAN_TENANT_ID`.

sections.heading: The numbers and where they come from
sections.text:
- **Seats** count active and invited users against the licence.
- **Settings** hold the numbers every score uses: the dimension weights, the score bands, the tolerance (failing share and failing records) and the severity weights. A change applies to the next analysis; scores already stored with a run are kept as they were.
- **Health checks** are measured by the platform itself and refresh every 30 seconds.
- **Policy pack coverage** counts the fields of the pack's classes, the rules that check them, the rules a run has measured and their failing records in the current state; a class is breached when one of its critical rules fails.
- **Digest numbers** are the landscape's own: the preview's numbers are what the email is rendered from.
- **Billing** counts resolved exceptions by tier for the month, on top of the base fee, from Meridian HQ.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text:
- **Platform admin**: every section.
- **Manage users**: users, roles, single sign-on, sign-in page, view as, share links, out of office, API keys.
- **Manage settings**: settings, billing, stewardship, configuration bundle, alerts, default digest, webhooks, digests.
- **Manage system**: licence, platform and updates, the diagnostics bundle, sandbox mode.
- **Manage rules**: apply and remove policy packs; anyone who holds view reads them.
- **View audit** (auditor): the audit log, and a person's activity in People.
- **Manage field mappings**, **manage systems**, **manage rules**: field mappings, reference data, rules import and export.
- **Trigger sync**, **analyse** or **upload** (SAP Basis, analyst, programme lead): start and schedule.
- Anyone who holds view reads the licence, settings, mappings, reference data, alerts and the default digest, read only.

sections.heading: Administrator training guide
sections.text: The course for the administrator and the SAP Basis colleague (install and first start, licence, users and access, connecting SAP, extraction and schedules, scoring and money, write-back, notifications, operations and troubleshooting) is the printable administrator training guide, `docs/admin-training/meridian-administrator-training.pdf` in the Meridian repository. Ask your Meridian contact for it if you do not have the repository.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.text:
- In every section table, `j` and `k` move and `Enter` opens the row in the inspector.
- `Esc` closes the inspector; the section index stays on the left.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **"... needs the ... permission. Ask an administrator to grant it."** Your role does not open that section.
- **"These settings are read only for your role."** You can read but not change them.
- **Health check warning "No email backend configured"**: digests and email alerts are not sent until the deployment's email settings are set.
- **Single sign-on test fails**: check the redirect address registered at the identity provider matches the one shown, character for character.
- **"The tenant is already in sandbox mode."** or **"The tenant is not in sandbox mode."**: someone else entered or exited first; the page reads the state again.
- **A digest shows Held back**: the tenant is in sandbox mode, so nothing was sent; the delivery log keeps the attempt.
- **The interactive API documentation answers 404**: `/docs` and `/openapi.json` are served only on a development deployment or with `MERIDIAN_OPENAPI_PUBLIC=1`.
- **A purge request**: purges are irreversible. The token only works after 24 hours so a mistake can be caught; the purge log keeps the record.

chapters.title: Preferences
chapters.summary: Theme, density, locale and time zone, start screen, keyboard hints, digest and what you hear about.
captions: Preferences belong to you, not the tenant. Every change is saved at once.
Theme and row density.
Number and date format, and your time zone. The sample line shows the result.
Start screen: open Meridian as another role's start screen. Your access does not change.
Keyboard hints, your digest, and critical findings at once.
What you hear about: the events that reach your inbox.
Out of office is set from People: who covers your approvals while you are away.
Inbox and triage settings decide what reaches your inbox and who covers it.
Your digest: daily, weekly or off.
Preferences open from your account menu, top right.

sections.text: Preferences is how Meridian looks and reads for you, where it starts, and what it tells you about. It belongs to you, not to the tenant. Open it from your account menu, **Preferences**, or with `?open=preferences`. Every change is saved at once.

sections.heading: What is in it
sections.text:
- **Display**: **Theme** (Light, Dark or System) and **Row density** (Compact, Default or Comfortable).
- **Language and region**: **Number and date format** (Browser default or a locale such as en-ZA or de-DE) and **Time zone** (UTC by default). A sample line shows the result: "Dates read 16 Oct 2026, 05:17, scores 71.8, counts 1,234,567."
- **Start screen**: **Open Meridian as** your role's default or another role's start screen. "It changes the next step on the landscape and the work it shows first. Your access does not change."
- **Keyboard**: "Show keyboard hints beside menu items and places".
- **Notifications**: the digest of your open items (Off, Daily, Weekly), "Tell me at once about critical findings" and "Also email me". **Inbox and triage settings** opens triage.
- **What you hear about**: the events that reach your inbox, such as run finished, score drop, new critical breach, batch waiting and mentions, each on or off.
- **Out of office**: set from People, Out of office, or `?open=away`.

sections.heading: The numbers and where they come from
sections.text: Nothing here changes a number. The locale changes how numbers and dates are written; the time zone changes the times shown; scores and counts stay the same.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text: Everyone sets their own preferences. The tenant's default digest and alert channels are set by an administrator under Administration, Default digest and Alerts.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.text:
- `Tab` moves through the settings, `Space` toggles a switch.
- `Esc` closes the panel.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **Dates show in UTC**: set your time zone here.
- **No email arrives**: "Also email me" is off, or the deployment has no email backend (Administration, Platform and updates, Health checks).
- **The start screen did not change**: the start screen is kept in this browser; another browser keeps its own.

chapters.title: Keyboard and the command line
chapters.summary: Every shortcut, and the command line that opens any record, rule, object or run by typing.
captions: Meridian can be driven from the keyboard. Question mark shows every shortcut.
The shortcut sheet: everywhere, go to, tables, the ledger, the inspector, the command line.
Esc closes the top layer.
Command K, or slash, opens the command line.
Type a rule id to open the rule.
Or a word such as approve.
Enter opens it.
G then W goes to Work; g then l, r or p to Landscape, Runs or People.
In the ledger, j and k move, x selects, Enter opens the row.
a accepts the suggested value, n marks not an issue, r accepts the risk, e exports the fix sheet.
In the inspector, the square brackets step to the previous and next row.

sections.text: Meridian can be driven from the keyboard: a whole ledger can be worked without the mouse, and every canvas and action is reachable by typing. `?` shows the full sheet at any time; the keys are the same on every screen.

sections.heading: The command line
Everywhere
sections.text:
- `⌘K` or `/`: open the command line.
- `?`: show the shortcut sheet.
- `⌘Z`: undo the last change (when focus is not in a text field).
- `Esc`: close the top layer: menu, then inspector, then the selection.

sections.heading: Go to
sections.text:
- `g` then `l`: Landscape.
- `g` then `w`: Work.
- `g` then `r`: Runs.
- `g` then `p`: People.

sections.heading: Tables and lists
sections.text:
- `j` or `↓`: next row. `k` or `↑`: previous row.
- `Shift+J` or `Shift+↓`, `Shift+K` or `Shift+↑`: extend the selection.
- `Enter`: open the row in the inspector.
- `x`: select or clear the row.

sections.heading: Work ledger
sections.text:
- `a`: accept the suggested value on the selected rows.
- `n`: mark the selected rows as not an issue.
- `r`: accept the risk on the selected rows.
- `e`: export the fix sheet of what is on screen.
- `f`: move to the filter chips.
- `⌘D`: fill the New value of the first selected row down the selection.
- Paste several lines into a New value cell to fill the selected rows.

sections.heading: Inspector
sections.text:
- `]`: open the next row. `[`: open the previous row.
- `Tab` cycles inside the inspector.
- `Esc` closes it and returns you to where you were.

sections.heading: Where the numbers come from
sections.text: Nothing typed in the command line is guessed: results come from the tenant's own records, rules, objects and runs, grouped by kind.

sections.heading: What you can do, by role
sections.text: Every role can use every key. A key that acts (`a`, `n`, `r`) does nothing visible when your role does not hold the action; the ledger says "Read-only for your role".

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **A key does nothing**: focus is in a text field. Press `Esc` or click the page, then try again. `⌘K` and `Esc` work everywhere.
- **"Select rows first: x selects the highlighted row, Shift+J extends the selection."** A ledger key was pressed with no row selected.
- **The command line finds nothing**: try a shorter word, or the record key as SAP stores it, with its leading zeros.
- **Keyboard hints are missing beside places**: turn them on under Preferences, Keyboard.

chapters.summary: Readiness by wave, gates, the receipt behind a no-go, balancing work and the board pack.

Open the wave and set its gate: min score, zero criticals, contracts met.

sections.text: You run the data programme: you need to know how ready each system and object is for the next wave, what holds it back, who is working on it, and what to tell the steering committee. Your start screen is the **Landscape** with the next-step button for your nearest wave.

sections.heading: Your first five steps
sections.text:
1. **Landscape**: read the sentence and press the next step, for example "Clear the 3 no-go objects in Wave 1: finance foundations".
2. **Waves**: switch the landscape to **Waves**, open **Edit** on the wave and set its gate: min score, zero criticals, contracts met. **Save the gate**.
3. **An object**: open a no-go object and read its receipt: measured, capped, by which critical rules.
4. **People**: see who holds the open work and **Balance work** if one person holds most of it.
5. **Reports**: schedule the board pack for the steering committee.

sections.heading: Your jobs and where they are done
sections.text:
- **Landscape readiness by system and wave**: Landscape, Coverage and Waves views.
- **Plan waves (objects, dates, stages)**: Migration waves panel, **Add a wave**, **Objects**.
- **Wave gate criteria**: Migration waves panel, **Gate**, **Save the gate**.
- **Gate status**: the Waves view, "Gate not passed, 2 of 3 not met".
- **Readiness certificate**: the waves panel shows the latest issued version and its state ("Version 2, waiting for signatures", "Version 2, signed" or "Not issued"); the certificate link opens it to issue a version, sign it or download its PDF.
- **Sign off a wave**: **Sign off** on the wave in the Migration waves panel (needs approve); only a wave whose verdict is go can be signed off, and any later change to the wave clears the sign-off.
- **Balance work between stewards**: People, **Balance work** (even counts, whole objects or by the assignment template), applied with undo.
- **Read data contracts and their breaches**: People, **Data contracts**.
- **Watch objects**: **Watch** on the object header for run, score and breach notices.
- **Export the ledger or any grid**: **Share and export**, **Export to Excel**.
- **Share a canvas with the steering committee**: **Share and export**, **Share this page as a link** (read-only, expires).
- **Start extraction and analysis, schedules**: System inspector; Administration, Start and schedule.
- **Reports and report schedules**: Reports.

sections.heading: The numbers you report
sections.text:
- **The shown score** is capped: 85 at one critical rule over tolerance, 70 at two or more. Report the measured score beside it when it matters; the receipt states both.
- **Value at risk** is from the cost model named in the footer; it is an estimate from your own cost settings, not a forecast.
- **Go, at risk, no-go** come from the score bands under Administration, Settings.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **The steering committee sees different numbers**: check which run each of you reads. The run is in the top bar and in every report.
- **A wave cannot pass its gate**: open each object named under **Zero criticals**; the critical rules over tolerance are listed in its receipt.
- **Contact**: SAP Basis for extraction failures, your administrator for access, the object owner for approvals that wait.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: data steward
chapters.summary: Accept suggested values, decide a record, work a rule at once, the fix sheet, and your draft batch.
captions: Data steward: decide the right value for each failing field.
Step 1, Landscape: press Accept the suggested values.
Step 2, Work: your rows, ranked by value at risk.
Accept a suggested value; the notice has Undo.
Step 3, a record: read the possible values and type the new value.
Step 4, By rule: decide a whole rule at once, or export the fix sheet.
By rule groups the rows to fix under their rule.
Step 5, Waiting for approval: your batch waits for a data owner.

walkthrough.text: Press Accept the suggested values: Work opens on your rows.
Select the top rows and press a to accept their suggested values. The notice has Undo.
Open a row without a suggestion, read the possible values and type the New value.
Switch to By rule and decide a whole rule, or export the fix sheet with e.
Check your draft batch: a data owner approves it.

sections.text: You clean the data: you decide the right value for each failing field, accept what Meridian suggests where it is right, sign off what is not a problem, and hand your batch to a second person. Your start screen is the **Landscape** with "Accept the suggested values" as your next step.

sections.heading: Your first five steps
sections.text:
1. **Landscape**: press **Accept the suggested values**; Work opens on your rows.
2. **Work**: read the top rows, ranked by value at risk. Select rows and press `a` to accept their suggested values; the notice has **Undo**.
3. **A record**: press `Enter` on a row without a suggestion. Read the possible values with their meanings, type the New value and press `Enter`.
4. **By rule**: switch the ledger to **By rule** and decide a whole rule at once, or **Export fix sheet** (`e`) to work offline and **Import filled sheet** when done.
5. **Waiting for approval**: check your draft batch under the chip; a data owner approves it.

sections.heading: Your jobs and where they are done
sections.text:
- **Work the ledger: fix, propose, not an issue, accept risk**: Work ledger and record inspector.
- **Accept suggested values in bulk**: **Accept all** on a rule, or the next-step button.
- **Build a fix batch for approval**: every accepted or entered value goes into your draft batch.
- **Undo a decision**: the notice's **Undo**, or `⌘Z`.
- **Comment and mention**: Inspector, **Comments**; type `@` and a name.
- **Watch a rule or record**: Inspector, **Watch**.
- **Fix the upstream object first**: the fix-order hint, for example "Fix Material master first: 3,640 upstream failures. Records there fail before this object can pass."
- **Out of office with a deputy**: Preferences or People, **Out of office**.
- **Saved and shared views of the ledger**: **Views**, **Save current view…**, shared with everyone if you choose.
- **Balance work in the team**: People, **Balance work** (needs assign).
- **Author rules**: Rules, **New rule draft** (needs manage rules).
- **Import rules in bulk**: Administration, Rules import and export; there is no link from the rules library yet.
- **See your own activity**: your row in People, **Activity**.

sections.heading: The numbers you work with
sections.text:
- **Value at risk** ranks the rows; it is the cost-model estimate of what each failing value costs.
- **Possible values** come from the rule; a value outside them still fails and is refused.
- **Suggested value** is the rule's proposal, "Blank when no single value is right."

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **The ledger says "Read-only for your role"**: you need the apply permission. Ask your administrator.
- **A batch comes back**: the approver sent it back with a reason; it is in the batch inspector.
- **A fixed record returns to To fix**: the next run still found it failing after it was sent to SAP. Check with whoever loads the file.
- **Contact**: the object's owner for approvals, SAP Basis for extraction gaps.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: data owner
chapters.summary: Approve or send back batches, exceptions, contracts, your objects, and who covers when you are away.
captions: Data owner: you are accountable for your objects, and the second pair of eyes.
Step 1, Landscape: how many batches wait for you, and your SLA.
Step 2, the batch: the changes and the approval trail. Approve or send back.
Step 3, Waiting for approval: every batch, grouped.
Step 4, your object: watch it, and apply the steward template.
Step 5, Out of office: who covers your approvals while you are away.
Contracts: approve them, never your own.
Exceptions: records signed off as not an issue or an accepted risk, with the reason.
Triage and SLA: the days to resolve and the escalation chain after a breach.

walkthrough.text: Read how many batches wait for you and press Approve batch B-241.
Read the changes and the approval trail, then Approve or Send back with a reason.
Every batch waiting, grouped by batch.
Watch an object you own and apply the steward template to it.
Before you are away, set who covers your approvals.

sections.text: You are accountable for one or more objects and you are the second pair of eyes: you approve or send back the fix batches stewards prepare, sign off exceptions, approve contracts and glossary terms, and decide who covers for you when you are away. Your start screen is the **Landscape** with the line "2 batches wait for your approval, SLA met on 92% of your open work" and the next step "Approve batch B-241".

sections.heading: Your first five steps
sections.text:
1. **Landscape**: read the line under the sentence and press **Approve batch B-241**.
2. **Batch inspector**: read the facts, the changes ("`MARA-MEINS` STK to EA") and the approval trail. **Approve** or **Send back** with a reason.
3. **Waiting for approval**: in Work, the chip lists every batch waiting, grouped by batch.
4. **Your object**: open an object you own; **Watch** it and apply the steward template to it.
5. **Out of office**: before you are away, set who covers your approvals.

sections.heading: Your jobs and where they are done
sections.text:
- **Approve or send back a batch (four eyes)**: Batch inspector, **Approve**, **Send back**. You never approve a batch you built.
- **Out of office: approvals route to the deputy**: Preferences or People, **Out of office**; the batch and person inspectors show the cover.
- **Escalation chain after an SLA breach**: Work or People, **Triage and SLA**, **Escalation chain** (changing it needs manage triage).
- **Create and edit a data contract**: People, **Data contracts**, **New contract**; the contract inspector.
- **Approve a contract (never your own)**: Contract inspector.
- **Contract versions and revisions**: Contract inspector, **Versions**, **Revise as a new version**.
- **Contract breaches**: Contract inspector, **Breaches**.
- **Apply the steward template to your objects**: the object canvas, steward template.
- **Watch your objects; subscriptions**: Object canvas, **Watch**; Preferences, What you hear about.
- **Gate status of your objects' wave**: Landscape, Waves view.
- **Sign records off**: Work, **not an issue** or **accept risk** with a reason.
- **Merge pairs and approve glossary terms**: an object's Golden records and Glossary tabs.

sections.heading: The numbers you approve
sections.text:
- **Records** and **Value at risk** on a batch are the records in it and their cost-model estimate.
- **SLA met** is the share of your open work resolved within the SLA days set under Triage and SLA.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **Approve is missing**: you built the batch, or your role lacks approve.
- **Approved values do not appear in SAP**: approval does not touch SAP. The batch is exported and loaded by your team's process; the next run confirms each record.
- **Contact**: the steward named on the batch for its content, your administrator for access.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: SAP Basis
chapters.summary: System tasks, connection tests, dry run and changes only, schedules, and failed jobs.
captions: SAP Basis: connections, extractions, schedules and jobs.
Step 1, the Basis home: each connection and what its last test said.
The last extraction of each system with its records, and whether it was analysed.
Failed jobs to triage, and the authorisation errors among the tests and jobs.
The extraction schedules, with the next run and the mode.
Step 2, the system: test the connection.
Step 3, the inspector: choose objects, dry run, then extract or extract changes only.
Step 4, Schedules: Changes only for routine runs.
Step 5, Runs: open a failed job and retry it.
Field mappings and Start and schedule are under Administration.
Configuration: what was read from the customising tables, and what could not be read and why.
Custom objects: Z tables and fields, with anomalies to investigate.

walkthrough.text: Read your system tasks: extract again, run analysis, extract a system never read.
Open the system and test the connection.
Choose objects, run a dry run, then extract or extract changes only.
Add a schedule in Changes only mode for routine runs.
Watch the jobs and open a failed one to retry it.

sections.text: You keep the plumbing healthy: connections, extractions, schedules, configuration loads and the jobs that run them. Meridian reads from SAP with a read-only role; it writes back only where an administrator has turned on live write-back for material master, customer and business partner, through a separate SAP user. Your start screen is the **Landscape** with your own home above the coverage matrix: **Connections** (each system, its connection state and what the last test said), **Last extraction** (per system, with records and whether it was analysed), **Failed jobs to triage** (a job that failed and was not followed by a success of the same kind), **Authorisation errors** (refused credentials and missing authorisations among the connection tests and the jobs) and **Schedules** (system, object, when, next run and mode). The next step names the system that needs you first, for example "Extract SuccessFactors", and **Your next work** lists the system tasks.

sections.heading: Your first five steps
sections.text:
1. **The Basis home**: read Connections, Failed jobs to triage and Authorisation errors first, then the task list: "Extract ECC production again", "Run analysis on S/4HANA sandbox", "Extract SuccessFactors".
2. **System**: open the system and **Test connection**. A passing test reads "RFC connection succeeded (client 100, 41 ms)".
3. **Dry run**: in the system inspector choose the objects, run **Dry run** and read the rows and duration; then **Extract**, or **Extract changes only** where available.
4. **Schedules**: add a schedule with a rhythm and the mode **Changes only** for routine runs.
5. **Runs**: watch the job line and open a failed job for its stages and **Retry**.

sections.heading: Your jobs and where they are done
sections.text:
- **Test a connection, health**: System inspector, **Test connection**.
- **Extract objects**: System inspector, **Extract**.
- **Extraction dry run: row counts per table and a duration estimate**: System inspector, **Dry run**.
- **Delta extraction (changes only)**: System inspector, **Extract changes only**; schedules in **Changes only** mode.
- **Schedules, retry, cancel**: the system's Schedules view; Administration, Start and schedule.
- **Field mappings**: Administration, Field mappings.
- **The read-only SAP role and the table reader**: `docs/sap/authorisation-role-template.md` lists the S_RFC function modules and the S_TABU_NAM tables; `MERIDIAN_RFC_READ_FUNCTION` in `.env` chooses `RFC_READ_TABLE` (default), `/BODS/RFC_READ_TABLE2`, `BBP_RFC_READ_TABLE` or `auto`.
- **Load configuration and compare with the target**: the system's Configuration view.
- **Custom objects**: the system's Custom objects view.
- **Watch a system**: possible through the API only; the System inspector has no Watch button yet.

sections.heading: The numbers you watch
sections.text:
- **Records** per extraction and per table, from the job registry; the Basis home's Last extraction shows the latest per system.
- **Failed jobs to triage** and **Authorisation errors** count what still needs you.
- **Areas loaded**, for example "11 of 12", and per area what could not be read and why.
- **Health checks** under Administration, Platform and updates.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **HTTP 401 or "Sign-in refused"**: rotate the credentials in Connection settings and test again.
- **"No authorisation to read this table. The user needs read access to it."** Grant the RFC user read access from the role template, then **Load again**. SU53 shows the failed check.
- **The table reader is refused**: set `MERIDIAN_RFC_READ_FUNCTION` to the reader your role grants, or `auto`.
- **A scheduled extraction did not start**: due runs start within 5 minutes; check Runs, Jobs and the background workers health check.
- **Contact**: your administrator for permissions on a system; the programme lead for which objects to extract.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: process analyst
chapters.summary: Blocked process steps, the what-if simulation, handing a rule off, and the process designer.

Step 1, Landscape: press Open PTP step 3.
Step 2, Processes: which steps Material master blocks, and the fields behind them.
Step 3, What if: tick the rules to fix and see which steps would be ready.
Step 4, the step: hand its blocking rule to a steward.
Step 5, the designer: map the fields each activity reads, then publish.
A step is blocked when a field it writes fails a critical or high rule, or passes under 70%.
Comment on a rule from its inspector to tell the steward what the process needs.
Related objects in the header show which object to fix first.

walkthrough.text: Press Open PTP step 3.
Read which steps Material master blocks and the fields behind them.
Tick the rules to fix and see which steps would be ready.
Hand the blocking rule to a steward with a note.
Map the fields each activity reads, then publish the model.

sections.text: You read the data through the business process: which steps of Procure to Pay, Plan to Produce or Order to Cash the data blocks, what fixing a rule would release, and whom to hand a blocking rule to. Your start screen is the **Landscape** with "Open PTP step 3" as your next step.

sections.heading: Your first five steps
sections.text:
1. **Landscape**: press **Open PTP step 3**.
2. **Processes tab**: read "2 of 4 process steps are blocked by Material master: PTP step 3, PP step 1." and the fields behind each blocked step.
3. **What if**: tick the rules to fix under **What if these rules were fixed** and see which steps would be ready.
4. **Step inspector**: **Hand off** the blocking rule to a steward with a note.
5. **Process designer**: map the fields each activity reads, then publish the model.

sections.heading: Your jobs and where they are done
sections.text:
- **Process readiness by step**: Object, **Processes** tab.
- **What if these rules were fixed (simulation)**: Processes tab; computed in the browser, nothing changes and no data is read.
- **Hand a blocking rule to a steward**: Step inspector, **Hand off** (needs handoff rule).
- **Export the as-is process**: Processes and the designer (needs export process).
- **Comment on a rule or a step's rule**: Rule inspector, **Comments**.
- **Related objects and fix order**: Object header, related objects; the fix-order hint in Work.

sections.heading: The numbers you read
sections.text:
- "A step is blocked when a field it writes fails a critical or high rule, or passes under 70%."
- Failing counts are records, and a record can fail several rules.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **A step you expect blocked is Ready**: its fields are not mapped to the activity. Map them in the designer; it shows on the next run.
- **Hand off is missing**: your role lacks handoff rule.
- **Contact**: the object's owner for priorities, the steward the rule was handed to for progress.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: auditor and viewer
chapters.summary: Receipts behind every number, four-eyes evidence, the audit log, a person's activity and share links.
captions: Auditor and viewer: read every number and its receipt. Nothing you do changes data.
Step 1, Landscape: the same landscape, read-only.
Step 2, an object: the receipt and every i.
Step 3, Approvals: the four-eyes evidence.
Step 4, Audit log: filter by person and dates, then export.
Step 5, a person's activity.
A share link opens one page read-only, as a viewer.
Every comparison states its method: the common set of rules and what counts as a change.
A rule's versions and history sit side by side in its inspector.

walkthrough.text: Read the sentence and the coverage matrix, read-only.
Open the receipt and every i: the arithmetic behind each figure.
Read the four-eyes evidence: who drafted, who approved, who signed off and why.
Filter by person and dates, and export it.
Open a person and read their activity.

sections.text: You read: every canvas, every number and its receipt, and, as an auditor, the audit log and each person's activity. Nothing you do changes data. Your start screen is the **Landscape**, the same one the programme lead sees, read-only. A viewer may also arrive through a share link, which opens one page read-only with the bar "Shared view. Read-only, as a viewer."

sections.heading: Your first five steps
sections.text:
1. **Landscape**: read the sentence and the coverage matrix; hover a cell for its reading.
2. **An object**: open the receipt and every **i**: the arithmetic behind each figure.
3. **Approvals**: in Work, **Waiting for approval** and **Exceptions** show the four-eyes evidence: who drafted, who approved, who signed off and why.
4. **Audit log** (auditor): Administration, **Audit log**; filter by person and dates and **Export Excel**.
5. **Person activity** (auditor): People, open a person, **Activity**.

sections.heading: Your jobs and where they are done
sections.text:
- **Read every canvas**: all canvases, read-only.
- **Audit log and export (auditor)**: Administration, Audit log.
- **A person's audit trail (auditor)**: Person inspector, **Activity**.
- **Open a read-only share link**: `/share/{token}`; the bar says "Shared view", and **Leave the shared view** returns you.
- **Export a grid (auditor)**: **Share and export**, **Export to Excel**.
- **Read comments**: Inspector, **Comments**.
- **Rule change trail joining versions and runs**: not joined yet; read the rule's **Versions** and **History** side by side.

sections.heading: The numbers you check
sections.text:
- Every object score has a receipt: dimension points, measured, cap and shown. The formula line states the weights, the severity weights, the tolerance and the cap rule.
- Comparisons state their method: the common set of rules and the change threshold.
- The audit log's **AI calls** list every call to the language model, which service made it and whether a deterministic rule answered first; prompts and records are never stored there.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **A share link says it expired or was revoked**: ask the person who shared it for a new one.
- **The audit log is missing**: it needs the view audit permission.
- **Contact**: your administrator for access; the programme lead for the run a report was built on.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: administrator
chapters.summary: Users and roles, single sign-on, settings, the stewardship template, and platform health.
captions: Administrator: set the tenant up and keep it right.
Step 1, Users: invite people and give each a role.
Step 2, Single sign-on: connect your identity provider and test it.
Step 3, Settings: weights, bands, cap rule and tolerance, cost model, retention.
Step 4, Stewardship: owners and stewards, check the diff, apply, close the gaps.
Step 5, Platform and updates: health checks and the platform version.
Support: copy the diagnostics from help. They hold no record values and no secrets.
View as a role: see the product as one role sees it, read-only, for support.
Configuration bundle: move a configuration between tenants, with a diff first.

walkthrough.text: Invite people and give each a role, scoped where needed.
Connect your identity provider and test it.
Check weights, bands, the cap rule and tolerance, cost model and retention.
Name owners and stewards, check the diff, apply, and close the gaps.
Read the health checks and update the platform.

sections.text: You set the tenant up and keep it right: who signs in and with which roles, how scoring and alerts behave, the licence, the platform version and its health, and the configuration you move between tenants. Your start screen is the **Landscape**; **Administration** is in your account menu.

sections.heading: Your first five steps
sections.text:
1. **Users**: invite people and give each a role; scope a role to one system or object from their grants.
2. **Single sign-on and sign-in page**: connect your identity provider, test it, then decide whether to require it.
3. **Settings**: check the dimension weights, score bands, cap rule and tolerance, cost model and retention.
4. **Stewardship**: name an owner per object and stewards per slice, **Check what applying does**, then **Apply**; close the **Gaps**.
5. **Platform and updates**: read the health checks and update the platform when a new version is available.

sections.heading: Your jobs and where they are done
sections.text:
- **Invite users, set roles**: Administration, Users.
- **Custom roles and scoped grants**: Administration, Roles and permissions.
- **Single sign-on**: Administration, Single sign-on and Sign-in page.
- **API keys**: Administration, API keys.
- **Audit log and export**: Administration, Audit log.
- **Export and import the tenant configuration with a dry-run diff**: Administration, Configuration bundle.
- **View the product as a role (support)**: Administration, View as a role; the bar shows "Viewing as".
- **Import and export rules in bulk (YAML and Excel)**: Administration, Rules import and export.
- **Govern share links**: Administration, Share links, **Revoke**.
- **See everyone's out of office**: Administration, Out of office, **End it**.
- **Steward assignment template, apply with a dry-run diff, audit the gaps**: Administration, Stewardship.
- **Licence, platform update, health**: Administration, Licence; Platform and updates.
- **Tenant settings (scoring, cost, retention)**: Administration, Settings.
- **SCIM provisioning and group to role mapping**: Administration, Users, Provisioning (SCIM).
- **Theme and compliance record**: Administration, Settings, Appearance and Compliance.
- **Webhooks, digests, the default digest**: Administration, Webhooks, Digests, Default digest.
- **Diagnostics bundle for support**: Administration, Platform and updates, Support.
- **Your own training**: the administrator training guide, `docs/admin-training/meridian-administrator-training.pdf`.

sections.heading: The numbers you set
sections.text:
- Dimension weights must add up to 100.
- The caps are fixed at 85 and 70; you set the tolerance: the failing share and the failing records that count as beyond.
- Score bands: target, warning and critical.

sections.heading: When something is wrong
sections.text:
- **Someone cannot see a section**: compare their role with the matrix under Roles and permissions, or use View as a role.
- **Email is not delivered**: Health checks, Email delivery.
- **Your first sign-in asks for a new password**: the seeded account and any reset account must change it first: 12 characters or more, not the email name, not a common password.
- **Sign-in events**: the audit log records sign-in, failed sign-in, lockout, sign-out and password change; filter by action `auth.login` or `auth.login_failed`.
- **The licence shows fewer modules than expected**: modules come from the licence in Meridian HQ; **Check with Meridian HQ now**, then contact Meridian support.
- **Support**: open help, copy the diagnostics under **Contact support** and send it with your request. It holds no record values and no secrets.
